scope: Live Loader Config query helper and the package-directory providers its exact entry lookup consumes

verification.native: 23 passed: query corpus, actual Loader/PluginPackages composition, live fiber disposal and failed apply, eager directory reads, real graph projection plus runtime-resolution/plugin-package/metadata consumers.
verification.scope_reason: The Config query reads Loader ownership and package lookup, so use actual composition for those providers rather than treating controlled entry snapshots as lifecycle proof. The directory-anchor fix also requires the direct runtime-resolution/package/metadata consumers.

behavior: Lists current Loader entries with tree-local patch ids and exact plugin names; reports schema/absent/unsupported/tree/inactive from active fibers, and preserves declared Config when apply fails. Runtime-created Agent preset trees are not enumerated.

Exact-name filtering and bounded numeric pagination follow Source defaults and error order. Entry detail resolves packageDir from its owning tree base URL and returns a self-contained draft-2020-12 document with recursive/loader-expression definitions, omission acceptance and limitations.

Reads the directory eagerly before returning the Promise analogue, while schema projection owns a shielded operation and its worker cleanup. Does not execute plugin Config validators or transform callbacks during inspection.

Fixes Python 3.8 Windows URL decoding that erased a trailing directory slash, then retains directory anchoring in native_package_dir. Normalizes scoped package paths like Node path.join; real Source packageOf checks include exports-blocked subpaths and query/hash URL anchors.

reasons: The first controlled fixture re-registered the same Cordis service; changed to the same query-context stub boundary as Source.
Actual Loader packageDir was missing. The retained diagnostic showed correct Loader base URL but packageOf miss; both URL decoding and directory-anchor handling required correction.
Three actual Source scoped-package results exposed mixed path separators; normalized the shared package-dir provider and reran all affected consumers.

limitations: Helper is staged for current inspect providers; production tool-cordis/creative package composition still awaits explicit current-provider registration and C9 promotion.
Directory-anchor tests cover valid file URLs, file anchors, scopes and query/hash. They do not establish new general Node resolver equivalence for arbitrary malformed URLs or unrelated routing modes.
